items.title: Cannot separate development from human rights and dignity: Former CJI BR Gavai
items.summary: Human rights cannot be separated from questions of social and economic development, former Chief Justice of India BR Gavai said on Friday. Justice Gavai examined the deep connection between fundamental freedoms and sustainable development goals. “A person may formally possess political liberty, but the substantive value of that liberty is diminished when that person is deprived of food, education, healthcare, livelihood, or the basic conditions necessary for living a life with human dignity. Rights therefore cannot exist merely as abstractions,” the former judge said. He was delivering the ninth Chief Justice MC Chagla Memorial Lecture. He stressed that economic growth by itself is insufficient to measure human progress. “When we speak of development, who the development is for, development towards what end, and development at whose cost?" he asked. Justice Gavai recalled his experience presiding over the Supreme Court's Green Bench. He described judicial decision-making as "walking the tightrope for balancing between ecology and environment on one hand and sustainable development on the other hand." He highlighted how the judiciary balanced environmental protections with community livelihoods by establishing eco-sensitive zones near wildlife reserves and phasing out human-pulled rickshaws in Matheran in favour of battery-operated vehicles to safeguard worker dignity. He emphasised that economic growth must contribute to human dignity. “Environmental protection must sustain the conditions of life across generations after generations. We hold the resources in trust for the future generations. Public institutions must enable people to participate in those choices and seek remedy when their rights are violated,” the judge said.

items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Friday (September 18) suspended the life sentences imposed on seven persons convicted by a trial court for the 2016 murder of BJP leader and Dharwad Zilla Panchayat member Yogesh Gowda, holding that they were entitled to be released on bail pending disposal of their criminal appeals. A Division Bench of Justice Mohammad Nawaz and Justice G Basavaraja passed the order on applications filed by the seven convicts (appellants) as part of their appeal challenging the trial court verdict. The Court also imposed various conditions for their release on bail. The appellants have been directed to execute a bond for ₹5 lakh each, along with two sureties for the like sum. They were also directed to deposit the entire fine amount imposed on them by the trial court, not leave India without the prior permission of the High Court and appear before the High Court or trial court whenever directed. Justice Mohammed Nawaz and Justice G Basavaraja Yogesh Gowda was hacked to death at a gym in Dharwad on June 15, 2016. A Special CBI Court in Bengaluru had, on April 17, 2026, sentenced former Congress MLA Vinay Kulkarni and 15 others to life imprisonment after finding them guilty of conspiring to murder Gowda. They were convicted under Sections 120-B (criminal conspiracy), 143 (unlawful assembly), 147, 148 (rioting with deadly armed weapon), 201 (causing the disappearance of evidence) and 302 (murder) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), The trial court directed that all sentences would run concurrently and ordered that ₹16 lakh from the fine amount be paid as compensation to Gowda's children. The present appeals before the High Court have been filed by seven such convicts (accused Nos. 2 to 7 and accused No. 18). Vinay Kulkarni has also filed an appeal in the matter. He and eight other convicts were granted bail by the High Court on July 31, after their life sentences were suspended . On Friday, seven more convicts were given such interim relief. Advocates Lakshmikanth G, Parameshwarappa C and Bhadravadi Siddeshwara appeared for the appellants (convicts). Special Public Prosecutor P Prasanna Kumar represented the CBI, while advocate Deepak Shetty appeared for an impleading applicant. [Read Order]

items.title: Retiring MP High Court Justice Avanindra Kumar Singh to donate ₹1.01 crore GPF savings to PM CARES Fund
items.summary: Retiring Madhya Pradesh High Court Justice Avanindra Kumar Singh pledged to donate his entire General Provident Fund (GPF) savings, estimated at ₹1.01 crore, to the Prime Minister's Citizen Assistance and Relief in Emergency Situations (PM CARES) Fund after his retirement. At his farewell function on September 17, Justice Singh also revealed that he and his wife Shivati Indra Singh have pledged to donate their bodies to a medical college after their deaths for scientific purposes. The announcement came as Justice Singh reflected on his 37 years of service, the people who shaped his career and the principles he carried with him as a judge. Reflecting on his retirement, Justice Singh conveyed he intended to continue working in a different capacity. “After retirement today, I will begin a new chapter in my life, and I will always continue to work on a new platform. I believe that we serve the Lord not only by worshipping Him, but also by taking care of all things big and small God has created on this earth,” said Justice Singh. Explaining his decision to donate his retirement savings, Justice Singh said, “As per office calculation, I will be receiving about 1 crore 1 lakh from my GPF account, which I pledge before you all to donate the entire amount as soon as I receive for the nation building in Prime Minister CARES fund. And this step is the beginning and not the end.” He also noted that the decision to donate his body was similarly rooted in a desire to contribute to society even after his death. “To give to this society on the principle that अपने लिए जिये तो कह जिये (If one lives only for oneself, can one really say that one has lived?), my wife and I have pledged and registered two days before to the medical college after our death, our bodies, so that it can be used for scientific purpose,” said Justice Singh. He credited his wife with suggesting both the commitments, saying, “I can say about her that every point of time, she supported me wholeheartedly.
